I am 57 this year, and I have farmed here in Quzhou for 25 years, so I do not like making big changes without seeing it work first. On my 14 mu, I will still spread the land across several crops. That way, if one price is bad or one crop has trouble, I still have something else. Wheat and summer maize are steady and familiar, cotton brings cash if the price is decent, and stevia is more of a market crop, so I will keep it but not put all my land into it. I have well water, but pumping costs money, and with some people working off-farm, family labor is not fully available, so I need a plan that is manageable, not too fancy.

For wheat, I will do what has worked for me before: normal October sowing, base fertilizer first, then one topdressing in spring if the stand looks good. I would rather not cut fertilizer too much on wheat, because if wheat turns yellow in spring, yield drops fast and it is hard to recover. After wheat harvest, the maize must go in quickly, so I will keep that land in the usual wheat-maize rotation and use simple tillage so I do not miss the planting window. Cotton and stevia both take more attention over a longer season, so I will not put too much area there. Cotton I will manage in the usual way with moderate fertilizer and a couple irrigations. Stevia can make money, but it needs careful management and labor at harvest, so I will keep only a small area that the family can handle.
